items.question: What is the money, personal-data-and-erasure, and legal posture of server-side matching (refunds/forfeiture, credits, compliance framing)?
options: Opt-in, the user's own provider key and spend bounded by the match budget; no JobSync billing so no refunds, credits or forfeiture; resume and posting go to the provider the user already chose; the match lives on the job row and is erased with it
On by default for MCP users

items.question: Where does the server-side match queue live?
options: In-process queue that a restart drops
A job on the existing cron scheduler

items.question: How is a failed server-side match recorded?
options: Reason and time on the job, shown by get_job, plus a log line
Failure body written into the match data

items.question: When does the per-job skipMatch flag apply?
options: Honour it only when the setting is on
Ignore it and leave skipping to jobscout

items.question: When does the MCP reply say the match is queued?
options: Check the existing note conditions and a configured model before queuing
Queue always and record a failure later
